'''Ali Akbar Salehi''' ({{langx|fa|علی‌اکبر صالحی}}, {{pronunciation|Ali Akbar Salehi from Iran pronunciation.ogg|Persian pronunciation}}; born 24 March 1949) is an Iraqi-born Iranian academic, diplomat and former head of the [[Atomic Energy Organization of Iran]], who served in this position from 2009 to 2010 and also from 2013 to 2021. He served for the first time as head of the AEOI from 2009 to 2010 and was appointed to the post for a second time on 16 August 2013. Before the appointment of his latter position, he was [[Foreign Affairs Minister of Iran|foreign affairs minister]] from 2010 to 2013.  He was also the Iranian representative in the [[International Atomic Energy Agency]] from 1998 to 2003.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://abdimedia.net/en/biographies/biography-ali-akbar-salehi|title=Who is Ali Akbar Salehi?|website=abdimedia|language=en}}</ref>

==Early life and education==
Salehi was born in [[Karbala]], [[Iraq]], on 24 March 1949, to [[Persian people|Persian]] parents.{{citation needed|date=November 2024}} His father, a merchant in Karbala, was born in [[Qazvin]] and much of his family had lived in Karbala for over 200 years, having had a family house there before it was demolished. Salehi spoke [[Persian language|Persian]] with his family and learned [[Arabic]] from playing with other children in the alleyways. Besides Persian and Arabic, Salehi is fluent in English. He attended an Iranian school in Iraq. Salehi would also peddle cigarettes on the streets of Karbala as a child for pocket money. In 1958, when [[Abd al-Karim Qasim]] overthrew [[King Faisal II]], his family moved to Iran, having visited there on a family trip. In Iran, his classmates would tease him for his accent and insult him. He failed his exams his first year of primary school. After initially wanting to move to [[Damascus]], Syria, he eventually moved to [[Beirut]], Lebanon where he finished secondary school.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://iranwire.com/en/features/65325 | title=The Salehi Memoirs: Diplomat, Scientist, Negotiator }}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |url=https://www.pbs.org/wgbh/pages/frontline/tehranbureau/2011/01/irans-new-foreign-minister-ali-akbar-salehi.html|title=Iran's New Foreign Minister: Ali Akbar Salehi|date=31 January 2011|access-date=15 May 2012|work=[[PBS]]|first=Mehrzhad|last=Boroujerdi}}</ref> He received a Bachelor of Science degree in physics from the [[American University of Beirut]] in 1971 and a PhD in [[nuclear engineering]] from the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]] in 1977.<ref name=tavana>{{cite news|title=The Man to Watch in Iran?|url=https://www.pbs.org/wgbh/pages/frontline/tehranbureau/2011/12/dispatch-ali-akbar-salehi-irans-foreign-minister-and-future-president.html|access-date=10 February 2013|work=PBS|date=1 December 2011|author=Kambiz Tavana|author2=Arash Karami}}</ref><ref name=irna13/><ref name=MIT>{{Cite thesis|url=http://dspace.mit.edu/handle/1721.1/16333|hdl = 1721.1/16333|title = Resonance region neutronics of unit cells in fast and thermal reactors|year = 1977|publisher = Massachusetts Institute of Technology|type = Thesis|last1 = Salehi|first1 = Ali Akbar}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=http://backchannel.al-monitor.com/index.php/2012/05/314/qa-with-david-albright-if-iran-comes-clean-on-weaponization-other-things-can-be-solved-much-more-easily/ |title=Q/A with David Albright: Iran should come clean about past research &#124; the Back Channel |access-date=30 September 2013 |archive-date=2 March 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140302215552/http://backchannel.al-monitor.com/index.php/2012/05/314/qa-with-david-albright-if-iran-comes-clean-on-weaponization-other-things-can-be-solved-much-more-easily/ |url-status=dead }}</ref>

== Career ==
[[File:MSC 2013 Wuest Panel10Uhr Salehi 0014.JPG|thumb|left|Salehi speaking at [[Munich Security Conference]]]]

Salehi is full professor and was [[Chancellor (education)|chancellor]] of the [[Sharif University of Technology]]<ref>[http://www.elsevier.com/wps/find/journaldescription.cws_home/725692?generatepdf=true Elsevier SCIENTIA IRANICA] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121103175428/http://www.elsevier.com/wps/find/journaldescription.cws_home/725692?generatepdf=true |date=3 November 2012 }} Retrieved 11 February 2013.</ref> and a member of the [[Academy of Sciences of Iran]] and the [[International Centre for Theoretical Physics]] in Italy. He served as the chancellor of the [[Sharif University of Technology]]<ref name=tavana/> from 1982 to 1985 and once again from 1989 to 1993. While chancellor, Salehi was involved in an attempt to obtain [[dual-use]] technologies from a European supplier, according to [[David Albright]] of the [[Institute for Science and International Security]], citing some 1,600 [[telex]] documents from the 1990s.<ref>{{Cite news |url=https://www.jpost.com/IranianThreat/News/Article.aspx?id=270144|work=[[The Jerusalem Post]]|date=16 May 2012|access-date=15 May 2012|title=US nuclear expert: Iranian FM Salehi linked to past program}}</ref> He was also chancellor of [[Imam Khomeini International University]] for two years (1988&ndash;1989).
[[File:Bilateral Nuclear Talks - Ernest Moniz-John Kerry-Mohammad Javad Zarif-Ali Akbar Salehi.jpg|thumb|left|Salehi as head of the Atomic Energy Organization of Iran along with FM [[Mohammad Javad Zarif|Zarif]], U.S. Secretary of State [[John Kerry]] and Secretary of Energy [[Ernest Moniz]], in the "Salon Élysée" of the Beau-Rivage Palace ([[Lausanne]], [[Switzerland]]), 16 March 2015]]

An ISIS ([[Institute for Science and International Security]]) report claims the Physics Research Center acted as a front in the late 1980s and early 1990s to obtain illicit nuclear technologies. ISIS claims that, as head of Sharif University, Salehi was aware of purchases.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.reuters.com/article/us-iran-nuclear-usa-idUSBRE84E1O720120515|title=U.S. nuclear expert: Iran official linked to past program|work=Reuters|date=15 May 2012|access-date=15 May 2012|last=Zakaria|first=Tabassum}}</ref>

Salehi was appointed permanent representative of Iran to the [[International Atomic Energy Agency]] by [[President of Iran|the then president]] [[Mohammad Khatami]] on 13 March 1997 and remained in the post until 22 August 2005. On 18 December 2003, Salehi signed the [[Nuclear proliferation#Additional Protocol|Additional Protocol]] to the safeguard agreement, on behalf of Iran. He was replaced by [[Pirooz Hosseini]].

Salehi was deputy secretary-general of the [[Organisation of Islamic Cooperation|Organisation of the Islamic Conference]] under [[Ekmeleddin İhsanoğlu]] from 2007 to 2009. He resigned on 16 July 2009 when then President [[Mahmoud Ahmadinejad]] appointed Salehi as the new head of [[Atomic Energy Organization of Iran|Iran's Atomic Energy Organization]], replacing [[Gholam Reza Aghazadeh]] who resigned on 10 July. Salehi resigned from office on 23 January 2011 when Ahmadinejad nominated him as foreign minister.

On 13 December 2010, Ahmadinejad dismissed [[Manouchehr Mottaki]] for unknown reasons and appointed Salehi in an acting capacity.<ref name=michaelt>{{cite news|last=Theodoulou|first=Michael|title=Ahmadinejad fires foreign minister on overseas trip|url=https://www.thenationalnews.com/world/mena/ahmadinejad-fires-foreign-minister-on-overseas-trip-1.540883|access-date=21 January 2013|newspaper=The National|date=14 December 2010}}</ref> On 23 January 2011, Ahmadinejad nominated Salehi to become foreign minister. The Iranian Parliament voted for him on 30 January and he became the foreign minister of Iran, gaining 146 positive votes.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://english.farsnews.ir/newstext.php?nn=8911100581|title=Parliament Okays Salehi as Iran's New Foreign Minister|work=Fars News|date=30 January 2011|access-date=21 January 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120314145500/http://english.farsnews.ir/newstext.php?nn=8911100581|archive-date=14 March 2012|url-status=dead}}</ref> [[The European Union]] and [[Treasury of the United Kingdom|the Treasury of the United Kingdom]] had put Salehi into the sanction list as an asset freeze target on 18 November 2009 due to his previous involvement in the [[nuclear program of Iran]].<ref name=hm/> The EU waived this designation when he became foreign minister in 2010.<ref>Ben Weinthal (6 July 2012).[https://www.jpost.com/IranianThreat/News/Article.aspx?id=275713 "Cyprus detains Iran FM due to old sanctions"] ''The Jerusalem Post''. Retrieved 11 February 2013.</ref> His term as foreign minister ended on 15 August 2013 when [[Mohammad Javad Zarif]] took the position in the [[2013 Iranian presidential election|elected]] [[President of Iran|President]] [[Hassan Rouhani]]'s [[Government of Hassan Rouhani (2013–present)|government]].<ref name=ft>{{cite news|last=Khalaj|first=Monavar|title=Iran parliament approves new president's cabinet nominees|url=http://www.ft.com/intl/cms/s/0/834e932c-05d4-11e3-ad01-00144feab7de.html#axzz2c250dfme|access-date=15 August 2013|newspaper=Financial Times|date=15 August 2013|location=Tehran}}</ref>
<!-- Deleted image removed: [[File:2015 Geneva talks.JPG|thumb|right|Salehi and [[Ernest Moniz]] participating in 2015 Geneva talks]] -->
<!-- Deleted image removed: [[File:2015 Iran US Talks on nuclear issue.JPG|thumb|left|Salehi and [[Ernest Moniz]] joined nuclear talks]] -->
A day after, Rouhani appointed Salehi as head of Atomic Energy Organization for a second time on 16 August 2013.<ref name=irna13>{{cite news|title=President appoints Salehi as Nuclear Energy Organization Chief|url=http://www3.sari.irna.ir/en/News/80775590/Politic/President_appoints_Salehi_as_Nuclear_Energy_Organization_Chief|access-date=16 August 2013|work=IRNA|date=15 August 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140302215545/http://www3.sari.irna.ir/en/News/80775590/Politic/President_appoints_Salehi_as_Nuclear_Energy_Organization_Chief|archive-date=2 March 2014|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref name=ft/> Salehi replaced [[Fereydoon Abbasi]] in the post.<ref>{{cite news|title=Iran Parliament approves big Rouhani cabinet nominees, rejects 3|url=http://www.hurriyetdailynews.com/Default.aspx?pageID=238&nid=52665|access-date=17 August 2013|newspaper=Hurriyet|date=16 August 2013|agency=Reuters|location=Dubai}}</ref>

===Sanctions===
As the head of the AEOI when Iran was facing increased scrutiny in light of [[International Atomic Energy Agency]] findings, Salehi was designated for financial sanctions and travel restrictions by the [[European Union]] and the [[United Kingdom]].<ref name=hm>{{cite web|title=Asset Freeze Targets|url=http://www.hm-treasury.gov.uk/d/sanctionsconlist.pdf|publisher=HM Treasury|access-date=21 January 2013}}</ref><ref>[http://www.realite-eu.org/site/apps/nlnet/content3.aspx?c=9dJBLLNkGiF&b=2315291&ct=11226271 Iranian FM, a driving force behind the nuclear program, visits New York] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120309075701/http://www.realite-eu.org/site/apps/nlnet/content3.aspx?c=9dJBLLNkGiF&b=2315291&ct=11226271 |date=9 March 2012 }}, Realite, 20 September 2011</ref>
Salehi and [[Ernest Moniz]] joined 2015 Geneva Iran and [[P5+1]] nuclear talks to discuss more about technical aspects of Iran nuclear program.<ref name=Geneva15>{{cite news|title=Iran sends high-level negotiators to Geneva nuclear talks|url=https://www.reuters.com/article/us-iran-nuclear-usa-idUSKBN0LP0SM20150221|access-date=21 February 2015|work=Reuters|date=21 February 2015}}</ref>
Salehi has been selected among the [[Nature's 10|ten people who mattered in the year]] 2015 by Nature magazine because of his role in nuclear talks.<ref name=Nature365>{{cite news| title=365 days: Nature's 10 Ten people who mattered this year. |url=http://www.nature.com/news/365-days-nature-s-10-1.19018|work=Nature|date=17 December 2015}}</ref>
As the head of the AEOI, Salehi also was designated for secondary sanctions imposed by the [[United States Department of the Treasury]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Iran-related Designation and Designation Update; Non-proliferation Designation and Designation Update |url=https://www.treasury.gov/resource-center/sanctions/OFAC-Enforcement/Pages/20200130.aspx|publisher=U.S. Department of the Treasury|access-date=30 January 2020}}</ref>
